modelingNotes: Common Market South End, 235 West Tremont Avenue, Charlotte — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-common-market-south-end.ts

The deli, bottle shop and bar that moved here from its first South End address in 2018, into what the press called a "new industrial-looking structure" of about 5,000 sq ft with a 2,000 sq ft patio (Charlotte Magazine; Hoodline, Sept. 2018).

WEAK EVIDENCE. No licensed photo of the building exists that I could find (Commons, Commons geosearch, Openverse, Mapillary, KartaView all empty within 400 m), and the 2016 lidar predates it (it shows an earlier 9 m structure on the lot). What is known: - OSM way/553077609 (outline, which takes in the patio). - NAIP (USGS, public domain): a pale grey flat roof about 17 × 16 m in the outline's east part, the patio (umbrellas, furniture) west and north of it, and a short shadow to the north that suggests a single tall storey, not the old 9 m block. Everything else is estimated or invented: the 5.5 m height, the wall and storefront colours, the corner entrance, and the sign (a plain panel over the corner, as STYLE.md asks when the lettering can't be checked).
Model frame: bearing 0; coordinates below are about (-80.86358, 35.21035); the anchor is the OSM outline's centroid.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-common-market-south-end", model "clt-common-market-south-end"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/c3921f733df14b41e1f6d15853cce7b343886f17/generators/clt-common-market-south-end.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
